name: Bloom: Content repurposing (blog → main image + 3 socials)

assignments.name: title
assignments.value: How consistent branding compounds over time

assignments.name: body
assignments.value: Most teams treat brand as a one-time project: pick a logo, set a palette, write a voice doc, then move on. But brand is not a deliverable, it is a system that pays off every time someone sees you. The teams that win are the ones whose every email, ad, post, and landing page feels like it came from the same place. That consistency is what turns scattered impressions into recognition, and recognition into trust. The hard part is that consistency does not scale by hand. As soon as you publish across email, Instagram, LinkedIn, and X, every channel wants a different size, a different tone, and a different crop, and the brand quietly drifts. The fix is to make on-brand the default output of your tools, not a manual review step at the end. When the brand layer is something your systems can call, every piece of content ships on-brand without a designer in the loop.
